layers.name: elevation
layers.title: Elevation
layers.description: Elevation is the land-surface height above the raster's vertical datum. It provides the basic context for interpreting relief, drainage, and where water is likely to move across the basin.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: slope_deg
layers.title: Slope
layers.description: Slope measures how steep the land is, in degrees. Steeper ground can encourage faster runoff and erosion, while gentler slopes are more likely to slow water and collect sediment.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: aspect
layers.title: Aspect
layers.description: Aspect is the compass direction that a slope faces. It helps compare sun exposure, vegetation and snow conditions, and other processes that vary with slope orientation.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: profile_curvature
layers.title: Profile curvature
layers.description: Profile curvature describes whether the land surface bends along the direction of slope. It helps identify places where flow may accelerate or decelerate and where erosion or deposition may be more likely. Curvature sign conventions can vary between tools.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: plan_curvature
layers.title: Plan curvature
layers.description: Plan curvature describes surface bending across the slope. It helps reveal converging terrain that gathers flow and diverging terrain that spreads it out, which is useful for understanding runoff pathways and erosion patterns.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: hillshade
layers.title: Hillshade
layers.description: Hillshade simulates illumination across the terrain to make ridges, valleys, and landforms easier to see. It is a visual aid rather than a direct measurement of hydrologic conditions.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: tpi_300m
layers.title: TPI (300 m radius)
layers.description: TPI compares each elevation cell with the average elevation in its surrounding neighbourhood. Positive values mark locally higher ground and negative values mark locally lower ground. The 300 m neighbourhood emphasizes smaller landforms such as local ridges and hollows.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: tpi_1km
layers.title: TPI (1 km radius)
layers.description: This TPI uses a broader 1 km neighbourhood to show larger terrain positions. Comparing it with the 300 m map helps distinguish local features from broader valleys, slopes, and uplands.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: tri_3x3
layers.title: TRI (3x3)
layers.description: The 3-by-3 Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI) summarizes elevation differences between a cell and its immediate neighbours. Higher values indicate rougher, more uneven terrain, which can affect access, runoff, and erosion.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: relative_relief_1km
layers.title: Relative relief (1 km radius)
layers.description: Relative relief here is the local elevation range (maximum minus minimum) in a 1 km neighbourhood. It highlights how much terrain variation occurs nearby and helps distinguish comparatively smooth areas from rugged ones.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: flow_accumulation_km2
layers.title: Flow accumulation
layers.description: Flow accumulation is shown as the upstream contributing area in square kilometres. Larger values identify places receiving runoff from more of the basin and help outline the drainage network.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: stream_network_25km2
layers.title: Stream network (>25 km2) over hillshade
layers.description: The stream network is extracted where contributing area exceeds 25 km². Strahler order describes the hierarchy of tributaries: when two streams of the same order meet, the downstream order increases. The map uses wider lines for higher-order streams. The corresponding vector network is saved as a GeoPackage in `Output Data/feature_vectors/`.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: distance_to_river
layers.title: Distance to river
layers.description: This map gives the straight-line distance from each watershed cell to the nearest mapped stream. It can help identify areas close to channels, although it does not represent the route water travels over the land surface.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: hand
layers.title: Height Above Nearest Drainage (HAND)
layers.description: HAND measures the elevation of each cell relative to its nearest drainage channel. Lower values indicate land closer in height to the drainage network, which can help screen for potentially flood-connected areas; it is not, by itself, a flood prediction.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: downstream_flow_length
layers.title: Downstream flow length to outlet
layers.description: This layer estimates the distance along the drainage path from a cell toward the watershed outlet. It helps compare how far locations are from the outlet along the flow network, rather than by straight-line distance.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: dinf_specific_catchment_area
layers.title: D-infinity specific catchment area
layers.description: Specific catchment area represents the upslope contributing area per unit contour width. The D-infinity method distributes flow between downslope directions, giving a more continuous picture of flow concentration than assigning all flow to just one neighbour.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: twi
layers.title: Topographic Wetness Index (TWI)
layers.description: TWI combines contributing area and slope to indicate where terrain may favour the accumulation of water. Higher values often occur in convergent, lower-slope areas. It is a terrain-based wetness indicator, not a direct soil-moisture measurement.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: spi
layers.title: Stream Power Index (SPI)
layers.description: SPI combines contributing area with slope to represent the relative potential for flowing water to exert erosive force. Higher values flag locations where concentrated flow and steep terrain coincide.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata

layers.name: sti
layers.title: Sediment Transport Index (STI)
layers.description: STI is a terrain-based indicator of relative sediment transport potential, combining information about contributing area and slope. It can help identify areas for closer erosion assessment, but does not measure sediment movement directly.

encoding.format: RGBA8: R=high byte, G=low byte, B=0, alpha=255 valid/0 nodata
